title: Voyeurism and stalking provisions - how effective are they really
p1: A person can be watched, followed, or secretly recorded without ever being physically touched. So why do many victims still feel the law is not enough?
p2: Many people assume voyeurism and stalking laws only deal with extreme cases. The reality is different. These provisions were created to address everyday violations of privacy and personal safety, including secretly capturing private acts or repeatedly monitoring someone despite clear refusal.
p3: But the real challenge is not just having a law. Proving intent, collecting digital evidence, and overcoming fear of reporting often decide whether a case moves forward. One surprising aspect is that repeated unwanted online contact, tracking, or surveillance can also form part of stalking behaviour, not just physical following. The law provides a framework, but awareness and timely action remain crucial.
conclusion: Do you think existing voyeurism and stalking provisions are strong enough, or does enforcement need to catch up with modern digital threats?
